mcp_tools.name: silo_search
mcp_tools.title: SILO v2 search: What is this name or id? Companies, funds and listed shares, with their stable ids (CNPJ, ISIN)
mcp_tools.description:
What is this name or id? Companies, funds and listed shares, with their stable ids (CNPJ, ISIN).

Example: /v2/search?q=petrobras

Kinds:
- any: Resolve a name or id across companies, funds and tickers.
- company: The company rows (id_type cd_cvm) of the lookup answer; truncated still says when more than 20 entries matched.
- fund: Fund name or CNPJ search, largest latest NAV first.
- universe: The research universe: one row per ticker+ISIN pair of listed shares and units.

Hidden parameters, in options: as_of (default none: every pair the tape has seen).

Read-only. The result is the v2 envelope as the gateway returns it: data (always a list), meta (resource, kind, request with every default applied, id_known, endpoint), and next_page_url only when more rows remain. To read the next page, call this tool again with only `cursor` set to the cursor in next_page_url. A call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached; nothing is cut silently. Errors come back verbatim (isError) as {error: {code, message, target, innererror}}; over_limit means narrow the request, not retry it. null means not declared at source: never fill it or read it as zero.

q.description: A ticker, ISIN, CNPJ, CVM code, or words of a company or fund name (every word must match, accents and case ignored). Default: empty: list the research universe (kind any or company) or every fund (kind fund, which refuses above its tier ceiling).

kind.description: any: exact ids, then companies, then funds (at most 20 rows). company: the company rows of that answer. fund: fund search, largest latest NAV first. universe: every listed share and unit since 2019-01-02. Default: any.

family.description: Narrows kind=fund to one fund family. Default: all.

limit.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

cursor.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

options.description: Hidden parameters of search. Leave it out for every default.

as_of.description: kind=universe (or an empty q): only the ticker+ISIN pairs whose first_observed <= as_of <= last_observed, dead names included. Survivorship-free. Default: none: every pair the tape has seen.

mcp_tools.description:
What did it trade at? Daily history (split-adjusted by default), latest quote, sessions, indices, B3 FORWARD prints.

Example: /v2/prices?id=PETR4

Kinds:
- history: api.quote_history: one ticker, oldest first, 1 year to the latest session by default, paged with the function's p_after cursor.

- session: One session's quotes from one price view (raw, adjusted false).
- index: api.index_history: one B3 index code (IBOV, IFIX, ...), levels as published (total-return indices, not adjusted).
- forward: api.trade_consolidated_history: one FORWARD-segment ticker; last_price is the close, ref_price is never a trade.

With no from, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

Hidden parameters, in options: board (default all boards: the series follows the ISIN across boards); asset_class (default all); fields (default core); date (default the latest session in the 14 days to today that matches the other filters).

fields defaults to core (concise rows); options.fields=all is the detailed form, every column the endpoint publishes.

kind.description: history: one ticker's daily series. latest: its newest session. session: every quote of one session (the seven price views in one). index: a B3 index's daily levels. forward: B3 FORWARD-segment prints (fixed-income ETFs COTAHIST does not carry). Default: history.

freq.description: kind history, index, forward. month: the last session of each month, selected from the daily rows (no interpolation; a month with no session has no row). Default: day.

adjust.description: kind history. split: close_adj (splits, groupings, bonus shares; no dividends). none: the raw close as traded. Every row carries adjusted (true or false); the other kinds are never adjusted. Default: split.

id.description: By kind: history, latest take a B3 ticker (PETR4); session takes a B3 ticker (none: every ticker of the session); index takes a B3 index code (IBOV, IFIX, ...); forward takes a B3 FORWARD-segment ticker. mcp_tools.name: silo_funds
mcp_tools.title: SILO v2 funds: What is this fund and how is it doing? Profile, NAV, holdings, debentures, FII properties
mcp_tools.description:
What is this fund and how is it doing? Profile, NAV, holdings, debentures, FII properties.

Example: /v2/funds?id=33000167000101&kind=nav

Kinds:
- profile: api.fund_profile: one row per family the CNPJ files under.
- nav: api.fund_nav: monthly NAV, quota, quotaholders and flows, oldest first.
- holdings: api.fund_holdings: the listed equities a fund holds (CDA), or with holding the funds that hold a ticker.
- debentures: api.fund_debentures: the debentures a fund holds, or with holding the funds that hold an issuer's paper.
- properties: api.fii_property_history: an FII's properties, every filed version, newest first.

With no from, a dated kind reads the last 36 months to `to`.

Hidden parameters, in options: holding (default none: what the fund in id holds); status (default all).

id is a fund CNPJ: 14 digits, punctuation allowed. Find one with /v2/search?kind=fund&q=<name>.

kind=nav columns are per family: a null outside the family's list is not applicable, not missing (coverage?kind=catalog, applicability).

FIDC delinquency (api.fund_nav, panel) starts 2013-01 and is on every row only from 2020-11 (regime break; coverage?kind=catalog lists it under regime_breaks). Through 2020-10-31 a fund with no tab VI row that month is null, not zero and not clean books; from 2020-11-30 it is filed on every row (a fund with none files 0). Never read a pre-2020-11 null as zero or fill it, and never compare a count of reporting funds across 2020-10 -> 2020-11.

Read-only. To read the next page, call this tool again with only `cursor` set to the cursor in next_page_url. A call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached; nothing is cut silently. Errors come back verbatim (isError) as {error: {code, message, target, innererror}}; over_limit means narrow the request, not retry it. null means not declared at source: never fill it or read it as zero.

kind.description: profile: one fund's registry row and AUM (with no id: the fund registry). nav: the monthly NAV and flows series. holdings: the listed equities it holds (CDA). debentures: the debentures it holds. properties: an FII's real estate. Default: profile.

family.description: One fund family. kind=nav: the series filed under that family (one CNPJ can file under two). With no id: the registry rows of that family. Default: all.

to.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

limit.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

options.description: Hidden parameters of funds. Leave it out for every default.

holding.description: Reverse lookup, instead of id. kind=holdings: the funds that hold this ticker. kind=debentures: the funds that hold this issuer's debentures (ticker, CVM code or CNPJ). Default: none: what the fund in id holds.

mcp_tools.name: silo_derivatives
mcp_tools.title: SILO v2 derivatives: Options, termo and futures: chains, histories, exercises, the DI1 settlement
mcp_tools.description:
Options, termo and futures: chains, histories, exercises, the DI1 settlement.

Example: /v2/derivatives?id=PETR&kind=chain

Kinds:
- chain: api.option_chain: calls and puts of one prefix on one session, by expiry, strike, side.
- history: api.option_history: one option code's daily quotes, oldest first.
- exercises: api.option_exercises: exercise prints for a prefix, oldest first.
- termo: api.termo_history: one termo code's daily quotes, oldest first.
- futures: api.future_series: one DI1, DOL or WDO contract through time, oldest first.
- futures_curve: api.future_curve: every contract of a root (id, default DI1) on one session, nearest first.
- di_settlement: api.di_settlement (a GET view): DI1 settlement rate, previous rate, open interest per session and contract, newest first.

With no from, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

Hidden parameters, in options: expiry_from (default today (the SQL's CURRENT_DATE): expired series are left out).

id per kind: chain and exercises take an option prefix (at least 3 characters, e.g. PETR); history and termo one B3 code (codneg); futures one outright contract (DI1F27, DOLF27); futures_curve a root (DI1, DOL or WDO; none: DI1); di_settlement one DI1 contract (none: every contract).

chain and exercises are cut by the SQL at a tier ceiling without saying so, so the gateway asks for 1,001 rows: a count equal to a tier ceiling (chain 200 or 2000, exercises 500 or 5000, or PostgREST's 1000) or above 1,000 cannot be told from a cut. chain refuses it (over_limit); exercises halves its date window and tries again, and refuses only a single day that is still cut.

Exercises are exercise events, not quotes. DI1 rates are % a.a. on 252 business days, as B3 settles them; nothing is derived.

Read-only. The result is the v2 envelope as the gateway returns it: data (always a list), meta (resource, kind, request with every default applied, id_known, endpoint), and next_page_url only when more rows remain. To read the next page, call this tool again with only `cursor` set to the cursor in next_page_url. A call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached; nothing is cut silently. Errors come back verbatim (isError) as {error: {code, message, target, innererror}}; over_limit means narrow the request, not retry it. null means not declared at source: never fill it or read it as zero.

Default: chain.

date.description: kind chain and futures_curve: the B3 session, YYYY-MM-DD. A date with no session returns no rows. Default: the latest session held (chain: the newest option session; futures_curve: the root's newest session).

id.description: By kind: chain, exercises take an option prefix, at least 3 characters (PETR); history takes one option code (codneg); termo takes one termo code (codneg); futures takes one outright futures contract (DI1F27, DOLF27); futures_curve takes a futures root, DI1, DOL or WDO (none: DI1); di_settlement takes one DI1 contract (none: every contract). Required for kinds chain, history, exercises, termo, futures. Default: none.

from.description: First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the resource's default window, counted back from to.

to.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

cursor.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

mcp_tools.name: silo_curves
mcp_tools.title: SILO v2 curves: What does the rate curve look like? B3 reference curves, their history and vertices
mcp_tools.description:
What does the rate curve look like? B3 reference curves, their history and vertices.

Example: /v2/curves?curve=PRE

Kinds:
- snapshot: api.curve: one curve on one session, shortest vertex first, fixed and moving vertices with rate_basis.
- history: api.curve_history: one fixed vertex through time, oldest first.
- vertices: api.reference_rate (a GET view): one curve's vertices on one session (business_days, calendar_days, rate_pct as published).

With no from, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

Hidden parameters, in options: date (default the newest session held for the curve (vertices: the newest in the 14 days to today)).

PRE and DPL are % a.a. on 252 business days; DOC is % a.a. linear on 360 calendar days, so its vertices under about 30 calendar days are not a rate level. rate_basis rides on every snapshot and history row.

Past the last maturity of the anchoring contract (DI1, DDI, DAP) B3 extrapolates: the long vertices are not prices. Nothing is interpolated: a tenor that is not one of B3's fixed vertices is refused with the list.

Read-only. The result is the v2 envelope as the gateway returns it: data (always a list), meta (resource, kind, request with every default applied, id_known, endpoint), and next_page_url only when more rows remain. curve.description: PRE: DI x pre. DOC: the clean onshore dollar coupon. DPL: the clean IPCA coupon (a real rate). Default: PRE.

tenor.description: kind history: the nominal tenor of one of B3's fixed vertices, in CALENDAR days (B3's vertex_code: 1, 30, 60, 90, ... 360, 720, ... 10800). 360 is the one-year vertex. Any other tenor is refused with the list, never interpolated. Default: 360.

mcp_tools.name: silo_macro
mcp_tools.title: SILO v2 macro: Macro series, inflation and its item tree, PTAX, Focus expectations
mcp_tools.description:
Macro series, inflation and its item tree, PTAX, Focus expectations.

Example: /v2/macro?kind=inflation

Kinds:
- series: api.macro_series: one SGS series by label or code, oldest first.
- inflation: api.inflation: the IPCA set by month with acc_12m, 3 years by default.
- inflation_items: api.inflation_items: IBGE's IPCA tree (weight, monthly change, contribution, year-to-date and 12-month change), 3 years by default.
- fx: api.ptax: one currency's PTAX, BRL per one unit, as published.
- expectations: api.focus_expectations: one survey and horizon across survey dates (the weekly revision path), median, mean and standard deviation.

With no from, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

mcp_tools.title: SILO v2 screens: Which funds look odd? Forensic screens: signals, not verdicts
mcp_tools.description:
Which funds look odd? Forensic screens: signals, not verdicts.

Example: /v2/screens

Kinds:
- list: The screens, one line each, with the family each reads and its SQL defaults (from api.catalog().screens).
- captive_vehicles: FIIs whose NAV peaked above min_aum while the quotaholder count never reached max_investors.
- delinquency_drivers: FIDC delinquency, first vs last observation in BRL and in points of NAV, the move classified (driver).
- dormant_funds: FI classes that filed every month of the window with zero subscriptions and zero redemptions (empty_shell, parked_capital).
- dormant_trend: dormant_funds counted at every month-end: funds filing, empty shells, parked capital and its NAV.
- evergreen_aging: FIDCs whose receivables overdue more than 1080 days stay a large, nearly constant share of delinquency.
- late_filers: FIIs and FIDCs whose monthly informe reached FNET at least min_days_late days after the cited deadline, in at least min_late months.
- overdue_securit: CRI, CRA and other series past their filed maturity whose newest filing still reports a non-terminal status.
- restatements: Funds whose FNET re-filings (versao > 1) in the window reach min_restatements and min_rate_pct of their documents.
- silent_filers: Funds CVM still lists as active whose last periodic informe is min_silent_months to max_silent_months behind their family.
- zombie_growth: FIDCs with delinquency above min_delinq_pct of NAV while NAV stays above min_aum, in one aging month.

Hidden parameters, in options: date (default the screen's own: zombie_growth the latest aging month; delinquency_drivers the latest complete FIDC month; restatements today; late_filers the newest month whose deadline has passed); months (default the screen's SQL default (12)); lookback_months (default the screen's SQL default: captive_vehicles 3, evergreen_aging 12, dormant_funds 3, dormant_trend 3); history_months (default the SQL default (36)); min_months (default the SQL default (6)); min_aum (default the screen's SQL default: zombie_growth 1000000, captive_vehicles 50000000 (BRL)); min_nav (default none: no floor); min_delinq_pct (default the SQL default (5)); max_investors (default the SQL default (10)); min_longtail_pct (default the SQL default (70)); max_variation_pp (default the SQL default (10)); min_volume (default the SQL default (100000)); min_delta_brl (default the SQL default (1000000)); min_delta_pp (default the SQL default (1.0)); min_restatements (default the SQL default (3)); min_rate_pct (default the SQL default (20)); min_days_late (default the SQL default (5)); min_late (default the SQL default (2)); min_silent_months (default the SQL default (3)); max_silent_months (default the SQL default (24)); dormancy (default all); driver (default all); modality (default all); family (default all).

Example: /v2/coverage

Kinds:
- freshness: api.coverage(); the source's as_of is returned as data_through (in v2, as_of means point in time).
- metrics: api.metric_coverage(): a (family, metric) pair absent here is one the family never files, not late data.
- catalog: api.catalog(): metrics, constraints, limits, applicability, regime breaks, screens.

Read-only. The result is the v2 envelope as the gateway returns it: data (always a list), meta (resource, kind, request with every default applied, id_known, endpoint), and next_page_url only when more rows remain. To read the next page, call this tool again with only `cursor` set to the cursor in next_page_url. A call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached; nothing is cut silently. Errors come back verbatim (isError) as {error: {code, message, target, innererror}}; over_limit means narrow the request, not retry it. null means not declared at source: never fill it or read it as zero.

kind.description: freshness: per dataset, data_through (newest elapsed period), complete_through, landed_at, landed_git_sha. metrics: filed span per (family, metric). catalog: the read contract as one JSON object. Default: freshness.

dataset.description: Comma-separated. kind=freshness: dataset names (funds_fidc, quotes, ...). kind=metrics: fund families (fi, fidc, ...). A name no row carries is refused, with the known names. Default: all. A JSON list; the gateway receives it comma-separated.

limit.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

cursor.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.
